verdicts.note: The axis is money and power in politics: PAC money, term limits, dark-money bans, RCV, direct democracy. The basis uses agency matters instead. Supervisor review of body-camera footage after use of force [S2] is police accountability. 'Continuing the office's current direction' is incumbency, which the experience axis already scores. The only political-structure fact in the dossier is that he runs as a 'nonpartisan independent' [S3], and that points the other way, toward pole_b. Under the Thurston Clerk and King prosecutor precedents, party independence alone is at most +1 low. His broad cross-party coalition endorsements [S2] offset it. No supportable score; drop.

The direction holds: harm-reduction and victim-centered training [S1], and success measured by 'prevention, recovery, and community outcomes' [S4]. But it is challenger platform language with no record, and the wording is qualified. Deputies are judged 'not just' by stops or arrests, and success is measured 'not only by arrests' [S4]. The same page also plans for staffing growth and an abatement and compliance team for crime-hub properties [S4]. High overstates a single platform statement echoed by one pamphlet phrase.

Outside WASPC accreditation, a policy review, published policies and a new field-training model [S1][S4] reform how the Sheriff's Office runs. They are not the money-in-politics or structural political reforms the axis names (refusing PAC money, term limits, dark-money bans, RCV, direct democracy). He states no position on any of those. He runs with a Democratic preference and party and labor endorsements [S2][S5]. Agency transparency and outcome reporting are already scored on spending (-1). Scoring them again on reform double-counts them on an axis they don't fit.
